title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: partial-coverage Cheon attack v2 (contiguous window, sequential giants)

claims.statement: For uniform s in [1,r), inputs T=[s]P0=A_1 and the auxiliary powers A_i=[s^i mod r]P0, i=1..n, on BLS12-381 G1 with n=2^20, the single-shot classical two-phase Cheon algorithm v2 in proof.md recovers s with success probability at least 0.39 using total work W(2^20) at most 2^123.777511 target-group-operation equivalents (time_log2 = 123.777511 = 123777511/1000000), including runtime factorization of r-1 (all prime factors < 2^28), generator and subgroup construction, three fixed-base comb tables, all baby and giant scalar multiplications, one mod-r multiplication per scalar update, hash inserts and lookups (1000 instructions each, open addressing with fixed 2^117-slot capacity), at most two window-start exponentiations, both BSGS phases, assembly, verification and output. The attack uses d=2^20 (the largest divisor of r-1 not exceeding the scoring n) and reads only A_1 and A_d. Phase 1 solves s^d = eta^k1 (eta of order N=(r-1)/2^20) by partial-coverage BSGS over a contiguous window of m=ceil(sqrt(0.40*N)) blocks at a uniform random offset - the giant scalars are genuinely sequential (one mod-r multiplication per giant, correcting the rejected v1 whose random-subset giants required exponentiations) - and the success probability is exact integer arithmetic: expectation exactly 2/5 (printed as an exact rational by the experiment at production parameters) with worst case 0.4 - 2^-118 for every offset, so no walk heuristic is used anywhere. Phase 2 recovers the order-2^20 component deterministically by full-coverage BSGS, and s=zeta^(k1+tN) is verified by [s]P0=T. Peak memory is exactly 2^124.0 bytes (the fixed 2^117-slot baby table, never overfilled); preprocessing is at most 2^21 target-group-operation equivalents (preprocessing_log2 = 21.0) and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Each fixed-base comb scalar multiplication is charged 64 units (2x its analytic cost); the sensitivity analysis shows the claim survives charging 384 units per multiplication everywhere (2^126.3). All preconditions are verified exactly at production parameters by experiment.py Part A (2^20 | r-1, verified factorization, zeta=7 generating Z_r*, eta of exact order N, zeta_e of exact order 2^20, exact coverage rational 2/5); Part B demonstrates the complete two-phase attack with sequential window giants on a 20-bit toy group with d=6: full coverage 200/200 exact recoveries with 0 wrong extractions, and the declared partial mode 88/200 = 0.44 vs the exact predicted coverage 0.40226 with 0 wrong extractions.

experiments.purpose: Part A verifies at full production BLS12-381 parameters (exact stdlib arithmetic): 2^20 divides r-1; the complete prime factorization of r-1 is verified (each listed factor proved prime by Miller-Rabin, product equality, all factors below 2^28); zeta=7 generates Z_r*; eta=zeta^(2^20) has exact order N=(r-1)/2^20; zeta_e=zeta^N has exact order 2^20; d-th powers of random scalars land in the order-N subgroup; and the exact integer coverage probability of the contiguous-window phase 1 is computed and printed as a rational (exactly 2/5) and asserted >= 0.39. Part B runs the complete two-phase Cheon attack on a toy prime-order group (20-bit, d=6 | n-1, N=174563) with the production-shaped giant structure: a contiguous window of m blocks at a uniform offset whose scalars are computed by ONE modular multiplication per giant (sequential update, at most two window-start exponentiations), in full-coverage mode (deterministic success 1) or the partial mode used in the claim (exact predicted coverage printed). Toy evidence is evidence at toy scope only.
